tasks.title: Railway trial D: build the trial corridor with the production line feature, ride it, judge it
tasks.notes:
GOAL. First real use of the production railway line feature: build the trial corridor in the live world, ride it end to end, and judge it with the owner. This is the representative build and the in-game judgement the code tickets cannot do.

READ FIRST: AGENTS.md; docs/plans/railway.md (all of it: what the 2026-11-22 trial found, "Owner decisions", "Ticket plan"); docs/agents/model-and-effort.md (builderTask dispatch gate; the owner must be present); rules/build-roles.md and `python3 scripts/build_roles.py --world southampton-build show`; rules/process.md; the railway line feature (lib/builds/railway_plan.py and the integration module) and its README or rules section.

PLACE: the trial corridor in world southampton-build, MC x 6740 to 7430, z -4400 to -3890 (cells 52..58, -35..-31). Ghost ground already exists for all of it. It contains one double-track main line, one double-track branch curve, one level crossing near MC 6980,-4343 (cell 54,-34), two mapped rail bridge spans (near 7285,-4290 and from 7415,-4107 to 7474,-4020), and 19 rail switches (a junction near 6820,-4085). The 2026-11-22 trial corridor was removed; the area is back to ghost ground.

DECISIONS TO HONOUR: docs/plans/railway.md "Owner decisions" 1 to 14. In particular: powered rail on every straight cell with a torch two blocks below; junctions, sidings and yards are NOT built (leave gaps for humans and report them); the line leaves gaps at the crossing and both bridges with end records (the crossing feature is built later by its own ticket); best effort, and fail loudly where a stretch cannot be made rail-legal.

STEPS:
1. Check the dispatch gate and the build roles; start under `python3 scripts/site_lock.py --world southampton-build run <owner> "<task>" -- <cmd>`. Plan with the production builder; read its failures list first. Dry-run before applying.
2. Apply, then verify by read-back (rails match the plan, every powered rail powered, torches present).
3. With the owner in the game, ride a cart end to end on each track; record where it stops or derails and why. Check corners, ascending rails, the speed on staircase stretches, the bed and slopes against the real surroundings, and the planting.
4. List the spots a human should fix (junction, the gaps at the crossing and bridges, anything that looked wrong), with coordinates. File any snags in the world repo (scripts/issues.py, the snag skill), not as tasks.
5. Write the findings into docs/plans/railway.md under a "Trial D" heading: what looked right and wrong, blocks changed outside the footprint (should be none), minutes and session tokens used (state the method), actual models and efforts, the ride result, and the owner's in-game verdict.
6. NEXT STEP, DO NOT FILE IT YET: decor sidings, yards and spurs (best-effort decor, clean unbroken runs only, never tied into junctions). The owner chose the study area: the yard around 50.91436,-1.45871 (MC 1901,-3299, cell 23,-32; 17 sidings, 3 crossovers, 2 spurs, 20 switches, a viaduct over the rails; probe extracts in the world repo under reference/vector_map/rail_probe_complex/). Say in the findings whether the line is good enough to start it and what its brief should contain.

ACCEPTANCE: docs/plans/railway.md has a Trial D section with a Cost heading and table rows and the owner's in-game verdict; the ride result per track is recorded; the human-fix list has coordinates; nothing written outside the footprint.


Owner decisions (2026-11-23, grilling): (1) At a junction on the main line, the line is laid straight through; only the side track leaves a gap, reported with coordinates as a job for a person. (2) Pass bar for the ride: each track rides from gap to gap on straights, curves and slopes with no derailing or stall. Any other stop is a defect, listed with coordinates. A defect on the main line means 'not good enough yet' and the findings say what to fix first. Planting and bed-look defects are noted but do not fail the ride. If the ride passes, the findings say the line is ready for the decor sidings and yards step. Put both in the acceptance and in the Trial D findings.

Returned to todo: Planner refused at the footbridge near MC 6872,-4194 (no deck height evidence); waits for structure evidence (#450) and the planner hookup (#451). Worktree .worktrees/384-railway-trial-d holds no code changes. Half-done on branch task/384-railway-trial-d.

tasks.title: First crossing feature: the level crossing near 6980,-4343 from OSM tags and Street View
tasks.notes:
GOAL. Design and build the first level crossing feature, in game, with the owner: the crossing near MC 6980,-4343 (cell 54,-34). Claude chooses the gates, lights and colours from OSM tags and Street View, then builds it using the crossing mechanism.

READ FIRST: AGENTS.md; docs/plans/railway.md ("Owner decisions" 7, 9, 10, 11); docs/plans/bridges-and-tunnels.md ("Already decided"); docs/agents/model-and-effort.md (builderTask gate; owner present); the crossing feature module and schema from the crossing mechanism ticket (lib/builds/, rules/feature-builds.md); the `snag` skill; rules/build-roles.md.

EVIDENCE ALREADY FOUND (OSM, node on each of the two tracks about 4 blocks apart, near 50.92340 N, 1.38633 W): `railway=level_crossing`, `crossing:barrier=double_half`, `crossing:light=yes`, `crossing:bell=yes`, `crossing:activation=remote`, description "Manually Controlled Barriers monitored with Closed-Circuit Television (MCB-CCTV)". The branch line crosses a road here; read the road data for the surface and width.

DECISIONS TO HONOUR: the rail feature trumps the road; the crossing feature lays the road surface across the rails itself; gates, lights and bell exist only because the OSM tags say so (barrier double_half, light yes, bell yes); their STYLE and COLOURS come from Street View, chosen in this build, with the frame ids recorded as evidence; no default style and no separate survey. The crossing is built after both abutting line features exist and joins their recorded levels.

STEPS:
1. Check the dispatch gate and that the line features either side of the gap exist (task 384 (Railway trial D) builds them). If not, stop and report; do not build the line here.
2. Get Street View frames: `python3 shims/streetview_sample.py --world southampton-build sample --cell 54,-34` (optional `--grid` and `--yaws`; it has no dry-run flag, so before running it tell the owner the source (Google Street View thumbnails), the cell, the number of frames and that they save under instance/streetview/, and wait for a yes; see config/system-providers.json for the licence note: do not commit the frames). Read the sheet. Note the barrier arms, lamps, signs, colours, and anything the OSM tags missed.
3. Record the evidence with scripts/decision_record.py (`evidence add`, `phase add`), write the crossing spec in site/builds/, choose valid block ids for bars, posts and lamps (iron bars and the other colour variants available in this game version; check lib/blocks/block_reference.py), dry-run, apply under the site lock, read back.
4. Judge it in game with the owner: does it read as that crossing, are the colours right, does a cart pass through. Fix by editing the spec and re-applying; file snags in the world repo, not as tasks.
5. Add a short Crossing section to docs/plans/railway.md: what Street View showed, choices made and why, what looked right or wrong, cost (minutes, session tokens, method), and the owner's verdict. Say whether the same approach should be repeated for other crossings.

ACCEPTANCE: the crossing spec and its evidence record exist in the world repo; the crossing is built, read back and judged in game by the owner; the railway findings file has the Crossing section with a Cost heading and the owner's verdict.

tasks.title: feature_build roofs: octant fit or fixed stair rotation for pitched feature roofs
tasks.notes:
From trial #257 parade snag S-105 (issue I-022 roof stair rotation; history #169, #310, #390). The owner saw poor stair rotation on the roof of Xionqi Hotpot (w122706803, a hand full spec built by feature_build) and asked whether it uses the octant roof system. It does not: octant is house_build's roof_fit option only (default columns, #415); feature_build has no octant code. But #415 also added align_stair_shapes as a final pass in feature_build (about line 598), so S-105 may predate that and may already be fixed.

Step 1, reproduce (read-only): dry-run the hotpot spec (site/builds/w122706803.json in the world) and count stair shape and facing mismatches with stair_effect_lines and roof_lint. If the count is 0, report that and stop: the owner re-checks in game after a rebuild (a separate world step) and S-105 goes to review. If it is above 0, diagnose which neighbour case produces them.
Step 2, decide from the diagnosis, and state the rule used: fix pitched_roof_states / align_stair_shapes for that case, or accept an octant fit per roof label in the feature spec by reusing lib/builds/roof_octant.py (fit_octant_roof, block_states). Note the hotpot footprint sits on a rotated diagonal; octant falls back to columns unless the footprint is near a rectangle, so octant alone may not help it.
Stretch (diagnosis, roof geometry across builders): ask before raising model or effort. Non-builder: fixtures and a dry run, no live apply. Acceptance: the reproduction count before and after, tests for the fixed case, and the owner's in-game check of S-105 after a rebuild.


Comments from the task-447 read-vs-build analysis (Papa John's, way 149814018, 2026-11-23; notes and prototypes in the world's site/task-447-papa-johns-read-vs-build.md; branch task/447-roof-surface):
1. Step 1 would count the wrong thing. Shape and facing mismatches are probably 0 here (align_stair_shapes exists), yet the owner still sees stairs that should be blocks: isolated interior steps (a stair with full blocks around it and no slope to climb, between two flat zone layers). Add that as a second reproduction metric. The live Papa John's roof has 4 (6518,-4568; 6518,-4567; 6519,-4569; 6520,-4570).
2. The octant fit cannot be reused as is: it fits one rectangle and one plane. A zoned multi-volume roof needs a clean surface per volume first (flat deck, gable or monopitch fitted from lidar), then the octant block choice on that surface. A scratch prototype recovers the real ridge on Papa John's (30.26 m, 0.40 m RMS).
3. The rotation worry is small: fitted per volume in the plot frame each volume is near a rectangle, so a roughly 34 degree footprint is not a problem there. Check this on the hotpot footprint.
4. Stair rule: stairs only on the rim or on a real fitted slope; blocks inside a flat volume and at a step between volumes. A neighbour-only test fails on rotated gables (diagonal steps look isolated), so the rule must read the fitted shape.
5. Related bug, fixed on task/447-roof-surface (4565137, not merged): with zones.levels auto plus regions, unused auto plateau levels clipped each zone's ridge rise to about 1 m. Reproduce stair counts on a spec with that combination only after the fix, or the roof is much flatter than the lidar.
6. Tree-covered lidar: a fitted surface also stops canopy noise becoming stair clutter. Pair it with trust checks (roughness, comparison with row neighbours, aerial green or shadow); staged tests caught 7 of 7 damage cases, but there is no real canopy case yet.
7. Suggested split: reproduction and metric; clean per-volume surface; stair rule; owner in-game check after a rebuild.

Update after the live rebuild (2026-11-23, #447 session). Merged to main: the ridge-clip fix (zones.levels auto plus regions no longer flattens a ridge) and the opt-in zones[label].surface "fit" key (lib/builds/roof_surface.py: flat, plane or gable per region, thresholds RMS 0.4 m and 70% of columns kept, else raw heights). Papa John's (plan w149814013) was rebuilt with it: 26 stairs (30 before), ridge at Y 41. Prototype scripts and block maps: world site/task-447-papa-johns-staged-test/ (smooth_roof.py with RULE=shape, step_rule.py, roof_compare5.png).

Owner review of the live roof, which is the real acceptance signal for this task: still stairs where blocks belong. The rule is: stairs only on the edge of a roof layer or on a real slope; blocks inside a flat layer and at a one-block step between flat layers; the rim rule that stops full blocks at the roof edge (roof_octant RIM_OPTIONS, #414) over-applies in houses, and feature_build's terrace-edge rule in roof_geometry.pitched_roof_states (stair at a one-block terrace drop, slabs at half drops and corners) has the same effect on rotated outlines. The owner wants an octant-style way to map stairs and slabs neatly for feature roofs, not necessarily the same code. Plan from the prototypes: fit a clean surface per volume (done, opt-in), then choose blocks from the fitted surface, with the rim and slope handled separately. A neighbour-only isolated-step test misfires on rotated gables (diagonal steps look isolated), so any rule must read the fitted shape. Overall verdict so far: notably better; flat front roof looks good.

Related tasks filed from the same review: flat-roof carpet finish (#455), volumes outside the way (#456), typology row front direction (#457), reapply lock loss (#458), read-step volume labelling (#459).

Wave handoff (files, order, worker brief, live-world protocol): docs/plans/roof-and-frontage-swarm.md.

Making it the default, house roofs included (the RIM_OPTIONS over-application), is task 462, blocked by this one.

tasks.title: Read step: label roof volumes from image and lidar profile, with cross-source trust checks (trees)
tasks.notes:
From the Papa John's review (2026-11-23, #447 session). Evidence and prototypes: world site/task-447-papa-johns-read-vs-build.md and site/task-447-papa-johns-staged-test/ (staged.py, reconcile_proto.py, smooth_roof.py).

Owner steer: the image identifies zones, lidar gives heights, flats and lows, a model makes a small per-building decision from the image with tokens used sparingly, and no single source is always right (trees can hide lidar and the overhead image).

Papa John's read-step findings: lidar in the plot frame shows four volumes (flat front 24.4 m; main range with the ridge parallel to the road at 30.26 m; a perpendicular rear wing falling about 0.6 m/m to the south; a flat bin store beyond the way). Tags give nothing about roof parts, no street view exists for the cell, and the shadowed street end hides the front in the aerial.

Needed: (1) segment the lidar profile along the plot axis into volumes (flat, ridge across the plot, slope along it); (2) one model call per building with the rotated aerial crop and the profile table to label each volume's roof form and colour (and dormer or bay at the front); (3) per-attribute trust checks: lidar roughness against a 3x3 median (clean real roofs: median 0.13, 90th percentile 0.21 over 150 houses; staged threshold 0.45; one real outlier of 0.58 at 6744,-5516 sits outside aerial coverage and is unverified), comparison with the row neighbours at the same position, aerial green or deep shadow; record agree, disagree or silent per source on each volume and fall back to the row or the class default when both sources are degraded; (4) test on a real canopy case.

tasks.title: Pitched roof edges on noisy lidar: measure the remaining full-block rises and flat stairs on West and Kiddle
tasks.notes:
Issues I-019 (Pitched roofs built from full blocks, no stairs or slabs; owner marked S-024, S-068 and S-069 not fixed on 2026-11-23, S-086 fixed; new agent snag S-118) and I-048 (Flat roof areas are built with stairs that gain no height; S-088). Records: python3 scripts/issues.py --world southampton-build show I-019 (and I-048).

Cause as far as known: pitched_roof_states (lib/builds/roof_geometry.py, from line 351) trims a terrace edge (#309) only when the cell has an even height, is not already a stair, cap or flat cell, has no higher neighbour in any zone, and has exactly one same-zone drop of one block (or two at right angles) with a level same-zone cell behind each drop. Three or more drops, opposing drops, missing backing cells, zone steps and drops larger than one block are never trimmed (a half-block drop gets a slab and is handled). Many edges on noisy lidar steps may fail that test; the share is NOT measured. For I-048, a read-only classification of West's 2026-11-21 plan found 16 of 760 bottom-half roof stairs with no higher cell around them (about 14 new since #311/#314); the rule that adds them was not found (untested candidates, test first: ridge caps #304, then terrace edges #309). NOT verified: whether the ragged brick-to-deepslate edge in S-118 is lidar noise or zone-edge handling; whether the opt-in per-zone surface fit already on main (commits 385bd57, a0d44d1, a7c178f; spec key zones.<label>.surface, read at lib/builds/feature_roof_zones.py about line 1031) gives West and Kiddle clean surfaces if switched on (West's zones have no surface key today, so this is a real test).

Scope: measurement and a recommendation only. Read-only: no live apply, no spec change committed, no code change. Non-builder.

Deliverable (a report in the repo, e.g. docs/plans/roof-edge-measurement-<date>.md):
1. Dry-run West (worlds/southampton-build/site/builds/west_w34391673.json) and Kiddle (w146985470.json) with python3 scripts/feature_build.py (dry run), then python3 scripts/roof_lint.py on both. State the exact commands.
2. Per roof, a counts table: (a) full-block cells that have a lower orthogonal neighbour, grouped by the trim condition that fails (three or more drops, opposing drops, no level backing, higher neighbour, zone step, drop larger than one block); (b) stairs with no higher cell around them, grouped by the rule that placed them; (c) brick cells on a zone edge with no brick orthogonal neighbour (the S-118 ragged edge), with a picture path.
3. Repeat (a)-(c) with zones.<label>.surface switched on for West's and Kiddle's zones in a scratch copy of the spec (not committed).
4. Recommendation: either (i) switch the surface fit on for these roofs (a world spec change, a separate world step, owner OK first) or (ii) a fix task naming the missing trim rules, each with the fixture that would prove it. The same function serves house_build (house_build.py about lines 772 and 778), so any later rule change needs a house dry run and the house_build tests; say so in the recommendation. The fix task is filed after this report, by the orchestrator, with the owner's yes.

Check lines (after a separate world rebuild step, the owner's in-game look is the snag review): S-024 and S-069 (West slopes and terrace edges): count (a) after the fix is at or below the figure the report states; S-068 (Kiddle SW wing ridge-edge caps): the same count for Kiddle; S-118: count (c) is at or below the report's figure; S-088: the 16 flat stairs of (b) are explained, and S-088 may also close earlier through the owner's review of the #314 check on I-048.

Overlap: blocked by task 434 (octant fit or fixed stair rotation for pitched feature roofs), whose step 2 may edit pitched_roof_states and align_stair_shapes. Task 447 (doing) does not need to land first: the surface fit is already on main.
